conceptual assets.information: The effective request to run the clock-enable ticker, derived from enable_i, controls whether the clock generator advances. It has no exit port because the RTL uses this value only to decide whether clk_en_o pulses are generated.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity: this configuration affects clock-generation behavior, is sampled into en at line 129, and controls counter advance or clearing at lines 130-134. Availability: en='0' clears cnt at lines 130-134, withholding all clock-enable outputs assigned at lines 140-147.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could force enable_i low or corrupt its sampled value in en, causing the generator to clear cnt and withhold required clock enables.

conceptual assets.information: Divided clock-enable events emitted on clk_en_o pace enabled subsystems and their operation depends on the correct timing of these pulses. The pulses are generated internally rather than carried in from an input port.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity: the critical timing pattern is produced by the ticker state and output logic at lines 131-147, so corruption can generate incorrect enable timing. Availability: the ticker clears cnt when en is inactive at lines 130-134, preventing pulses on clk_en_o at lines 140-147.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could disable the ticker or corrupt its timing state, causing incorrect or missing clock-enable events for downstream logic.

considered, not kept.reason: The clock/reset rule excludes reset requests, reset synchronizers, reset-release state, and reset outputs; lines 42-73 only combine, register, synchronize, or release resets.
The clock and reset inputs only time or initialize the ticker and are excluded by the clock/reset rule; this use appears at lines 106-107 and 122-128.
